assessment.rationale: Smart collars measuring heart rate exist, but none validly tracks pain and mood, and connected-device penetration is about 3 percent, so the Main KPI of 300,000,000 pets monitored is unmet. Invoxia's Minitailz collar reports heartbeat detection F1 of about 98 percent on 40 dogs in a vendor-linked preprint (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.06.09.544347.full.pdf), and PetPace heart rate matched Holter ECG in ten dogs, but its pain score has no published validation (https://phaidra.vetmeduni.ac.at/api/object/o:744/download). Accelerometer work tracks activity in osteoarthritic dogs and cats, while no fully validated system for chronic pain in cats exists and no validated wearable mood detection was found (https://www.lido-dtp.ac.uk/news/evelyn-maniaki-accelerometer-derived-classifiers-early-detection-degenerative-joint-disease). The largest tracker, Tractive with Whistle, had about 1.4 million users in 2025, against about 843 million owned dogs and cats (https://www.kenresearch.com/industry-reports/global-pet-wearables-market). Honest limit: GPS, activity and heart-rate collars are known answers; validated pain and affect measurement and low-cost reach are open.

additionalSearches.query: Invoxia Minitailz heart rate collar validation study; PetPace collar vital signs pain score validation
additionalSearches.finding: PetPace heart rate matched Holter ECG in 10 dogs (61 vs 62 bpm); no published validation of its pain score; Invoxia preprint F1 98 percent on 40 dogs.

additionalSearches.finding: About 843 million owned dogs and cats in 2025 with about 2.9 percent connected-device penetration; Tractive over 1.4 million users after acquiring Whistle.

additionalSearches.finding: No fully validated system for chronic DJD pain in cats; accelerometers track activity; no validated wearable emotion detection found.
